To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the C- 151T polymorphism in the early growth factor-1 (EGR-1) gene was significantly associated with lipid variables in control subjects.

two novel polymorphisms in exon 2 and in the 3' flanking region of EGR-1 have been identified, and that the –151T polymorphism was associated with lower lipid levels and a higher ratio between high- and low-density lipoproteins in control subjects not taking hypolypidemic drugs.

we have identified two polymorphisms of the human early growth response protein 1 (EGR-1) gene and found a possible association of one of these polymorphisms with lipid variables in healthy individuals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of a polymorphism in the promoter region of the EGF-1 gene and its association with lipid metabolism.
the role of genetic variants for lipid variables and their possible association with the predisposition to cardiovascular disease.
the identification and characterization of genetic variants of the EGR1 gene, which may contribute to atherosclerosis and myocardial infarctions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the C- 151T polymorphism may be associated with a lower plasma level of lipids and lipoproteins in the control subjects.
the –151T polymorphism in the EGR- 1 gene may have a role in modifying plasma lipid levels.
the –151T polymorphism may be associated with a lower lipid concentration in the blood and thus may have protective effects against coronary heart disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the EGR1-151T polymorphisms may be involved in the predisposition to coronary heart disease and that the C-allele may be associated with a higher risk for the development of atheromatosis.
the C- 151T polymorphism in the 5' flanking region of EGR-1 is significantly associated with lipid variables.
EGR1 may play an indirect role in atherosclerosis by regulating genes that are involved in the lipid metabolism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we identified the first two polymorphisms of the EGR1 gene, which may be associated with lipid variables in the human population.
the EGR- 1 gene may contribute, at least in part, to the development of atherothrombotic disease by influencing lipid levels.
we identified two new polymorphisms in EGR1 gene, and that these polymorphisms are in strong linkage disequilibrium with each other.
